summary: W45 shares immutable file-backed rigid parts across definitions and copied readers, preserves inline and placeholder fallback, and prevents in-flight cache reads from publishing in the wrong generation. Known queued skeletal and skinned payloads retain their parent allocations until discard or clear. The rigid cache table, control and parts allocations match independent Release observations before and after clear. Three actual rigid species preserve their earlier data through a resource reload and recover their original draw hashes on restore. All 46 Release regression groups, 12 related tests, scoped native startup, inventory/appearance input and resource reload pass.
